title: manni tracevals calibration labels
description: Ground truth for `manni tracevals calibrate`: what a human decided a given eval should have produced on a given trace. A sidecar rather than an eval field, because a label belongs to a corpus and a reviewer, not to the artifact — and because the eval vocabulary is docmeta's, vendored byte-identical, with `inlineEval` closed to additions (ADR 01010).

version.description: Format version. Pinned so a future shape change is an explicit migration rather than a silently-reinterpreted file.

labels.description: One entry per (trace, artifact, eval) you have judged by hand.

trace.description: Path to the trace file, resolved against this file's own directory — not the working directory.

artifact.description: Artifact name as the report shows it: a skill name, a subagent_type, or a project-rules filename such as CLAUDE.md.

type.description: Optional disambiguator, needed when one name resolves to two kinds of artifact — a skill and an agent, or a skill and the slash command that types it. Every `ArtifactType` the resolver can produce belongs here: a label whose type this rejects has no way to name the artifact it means.

eval.description: The eval's id. Shorthand entries with no declared id get a positional one (eval-1, eval-2, ...), so labelling those is only as stable as the order they are written in.

expected.description: What you decided. `needs-review` means you found it genuinely ambiguous and want the tool to defer too.

note.description: Why you decided that. Carried into the disagreement report, where it is the whole reason a disagreement is actionable.
